subject: Dedicated capacity: commit definitions, throughput SLOs and redline questions
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <procurement@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Atlas Health Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redlines to Dedicated Capacity Exhibit

Karthik,

Thanks for the draft Exhibit for Dedicated capacity. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed and have three principal areas that need clearer language before we can move to signature:

1) Capacity unit definition: your Exhibit uses the term "Reserved Capacity Unit (RCU)" but the redline we received from your team doesn't define the baseline hardware or throughput assumptions. We need an objective, measurable definition (e.g., GPU type or equivalent, baseline token/sec throughput at 2k context) so we can size ops and budget our usage.

2) Throughput guarantees and measurement windows: the SLA currently references a monthly availability % but is vague on how you measure "throughput availability" for pool-based capacity. Is this measured as aggregate pool throughput, per-GPU, or per-request? Also please define the sampling window (5-min rolling? 1-hour?).

3) Service credits and caps: our legal team wants the remedy calculation to be explicit (how credits scale with minutes of degraded throughput) and a clear cap. The draft has an open-ended remedy clause which is a red flag.

I've attached our annotated redlines (AtlasHealth_Redlines_v3.pdf).

We're generally excited about the dedicated option — the main blocker is aligning on deterministic measurement and reasonable financial remedies so our compliance team can sign off. Happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Atlas Health

Attachment: AtlasHealth_Redlines_v3.pdf (annotated redlines, 38KB stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Olivia Chen <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-02-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redlines to Dedicated Capacity Exhibit

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detailed pass and the attachment. Short answers up front, then proposed language for the contract team to consider: 

Quick summary: we can provide a clear RCU definition, an explicit measurement approach for pool throughput, and a tiered service credit schedule with a negotiated cap. Below is the proposal we discussed internally. If this looks acceptable I'll loop in Marissa (legal) to finalize redline language.

Proposed definitions and terms:
- Reserved Capacity Unit ("RCU"): one RCU equals the reserved capacity equivalent of a single NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU (or equivalent) in our Dedicated GPU pool, normalized to a baseline small LLM generation workload: baseline throughput = 100 tokens/sec at 2k context for the reference model. Customers may map model variants to RCUs using Redwood's model-profile mapping table (we'll include the table as an annex).

- Measurement: "Pool Throughput Availability" is measured as the percentage of 5-minute rolling intervals in a monthly billing cycle where aggregate pool throughput for the customer's reserved RCUs is at or above 90% of the baseline throughput. Aggregate pool throughput is computed as the sum of actual tokens/sec served by the customer's reserved GPUs (or equivalent vGPU allocations) across the Dedicated pool. Measurement will be calculated at the load balancer/ingress layer and reconciled against server-side telemetry.

- SLA and service credits (draft):
  * If Pool Throughput Availability < 99.9% for the monthly billing cycle: customer may request a service credit equal to 5% of that month's Reserved Capacity fee.
  * If Pool Throughput Availability < 99.0%: credit = 15% of that month's Reserved Capacity fee.
  * If Pool Throughput Availability < 95.0%: credit = 30% of that month's Reserved Capacity fee.
  * Credits are calculated on the Reserved Capacity component of the monthly invoice only and cannot exceed 50% of that month's Reserved Capacity fee.

- Measurement disputes: either party can request an audit within 30 days of invoice; if Redwood's measurement is found incorrect, Redwood will apply the appropriate credit and reimburse audit cost if mismeasurement > 2%.

Commercial: for a 24-month reserved commit we can extend a 15% discount on the Reserved Capacity fees (baseline). We'll propose commit tiers in the SOW for 100/250/400 RCUs monthly to simplify forecasting.

Next steps: I'll draft contract language for Marissa and share a DocuSign-ready exhibit. If you want a technical call, Aditya (cc'd) can run through the measurement telemetry.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-02-27T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Redlines to Dedicated Capacity Exhibit

Karthik — adding legal notes for the redline pass. Please incorporate these into the contract draft before sending to Atlas: 

1) Definition clarity: the RCU definition must include an explicit mapping table and a process for how equivalence is updated (e.g., new GPU generations) — include a "Model/Hardware Equivalence Annex" with versioned entries.

2) Measurement windows: 5-minute rolling average is acceptable, but we need to exclude scheduled maintenance windows and customer-induced throttling. Add a clause requiring 48-hour advance notice for scheduled maint.

3) Service credit cap & mitigation: we should cap credits at 50% of Reserved Capacity fee (matches Karthik). Add a clause that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for SLA breaches ("no termination right solely for SLA breach"). Also add force majeure carve-outs and reasonable mitigation obligations (e.g., priority bug fixes).

4) Audit & data access: define telemetry export formats and retention window (we typically provide 90 days of detailed telemetry). Legal prefers a 30-day dispute window — matches Karthik's suggestion.

I'll prepare redline snippets for the Exhibit and SLA Annex. Give me the RCU mapping table and the telemetry schema so I can reference them.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <procurement@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Atlas Health Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redlines to Dedicated Capacity Exhibit

Karthik / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete proposals. A few clarifying questions from our side before we commit: 

- The RCU baseline references A100 80GB. For procurement we need to confirm whether the Exhibit allows Redwood to substitute "equivalent" hardware without customer consent. Please add language that substitutions must be performance-equivalent and notify customer 30 days prior to substitution.

- Measurement: how do you treat transient spikes and backpressure? If the pool is temporarily saturated but autoscaling or burst capacity alleviates within 10 minutes, does that count as a breach? We prefer a design that accounts for short transient blips.

- Credits cap: Atlas counter-proposes a cap equal to 100% of the Reserved Capacity fee for the month; our legal team is reluctant to accept a 50% cap. Can you explain the operational risk that motivates Redwood's cap?

Commercial ask: given our 24-month commitment and the size of the deal (targeting 400 RCUs/mo), Atlas requests a 20% discount and a 12-week implementation SLA in the SOW (GPU pool availability, onboarding playbook, and runbook handoff).

We can do a sync tomorrow to resolve these items.

Regards,
Olivia Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Atlas Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Olivia Chen <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-03-02T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redlines to Dedicated Capacity Exhibit — counteroffer and next steps

Olivia — thanks, and great questions. Below are clarifications and a commercial counteroffer from Redwood. If acceptable, Marissa will fold this into the revised Exhibit and SLA Annex (I'll include the RCU mapping table and telemetry schema).

RCU substitution: Redwood can substitute equivalent hardware but only when replacement provides equal-or-better baseline throughput. We will notify the customer 30 days prior to substitution and provide performance test results for the new hardware. If the customer disagrees, they may request a remediation plan or choose to continue on current hardware until end of that quarter; this will be captured in the Exhibit.

Transient spikes / backpressure: measurement uses 5-minute rolling intervals and we will disregard single 5-minute intervals where end-to-end latency exceeds a threshold due to customer-side throttling or misrouted traffic. Brief autoscale-triggered saturation that is resolved within two consecutive 5-minute intervals will be excluded from breach calculation. We'll document the exact exclusion rules in the telemetry annex.

Credits cap: Redwood's 50% cap reflects the fact that Reserved Capacity fees pay for dedicated physical resources and headroom. A higher cap exposes our hardware and placement economics. That said, to reach agreement we can increase to a 75% cap for a 24-month commit on the following commercial terms: 
  * 24-month reserved commit at 400 RCUs/month
  * Discount: 18% off baseline Reserved Capacity fees
  * Onboarding: 10-week implementation SLA with onboarding playbook and two 2-hour knowledge-transfer sessions (Aditya to lead ops onboarding)
  * SLA credits measured monthly; credits capped at 75% of Reserved Capacity fee for the month

If Atlas requests the 20% discount and a 12-week SLA, we can instead match 20% discount but require a 30% increase to the onboarding professional services fee to cover the additional program management and expedited provisioning work.

Next steps: I'll draft the revised Exhibit and include the attachments: SLA_Annex_RCU_definitions.docx (RCU mapping, telemetry schema, exclusion rules) and a DocuSign-ready SOW. Marissa — please advise on any further legal edits and I'll send the consolidated package to Olivia.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
